criterio.pergunta: Is the 4-6% (test) and 5-6% (validation, g=5) gap between the whole-block Monte Carlo (continuous area, variant C of montecarlo_retencao_r3_g5.py) and the real nodal retention (20 seeds, varredura_split_geometria.py/EDT) 'granularity' (node vs block effect, not measured), or is it the protocol's trimming rule (an effect already captured by the exact sequential trimming over real nodes)?
criterio.hipotese: An MC run over NODE POSITIONS of the actual 3600x3600 grid (reconstructed from the run JSON, split_espacial_3vias_exato/cKDTree, rule 70/15/remainder to test, buffer b=2km, sequential trimming validation-first-then-test, EXACTLY as in the protocol) converges, with N>=50 permutations, to the same mean retention as the actual nodal retention (20 seeds); the 4-6%/5-6% gap lies entirely on the block-MC side (continuous-area approximation + generic block geometry per city, without the actual node discretisation or the sequential rule applied per node).
criterio.limiar_de_aceitacao: if |media(MC_nodal, N>=50) - media(nodal_real, 20 seeds)| / media(nodal_real) < 0.01 (1%) in ALL tested cells (g10: 4 cities; g5: bauru + 3 cities geometry only): the gap is attributed to the trimming rule/block abstraction of the continuous MC, NOT to granularity -- the granularity sentence is removed from the text.
criterio.o_que_refuta: if in ANY cell |MC_nodal - nodal_real|/nodal_real >= 0.01: granularity (or another effect not captured by the nodal MC with the same rule) remains without a measured explanation and the corresponding gap remains unattributed; the granularity sentence can only be removed, not replaced, without an additional measured cause.

veredito_vs_criterio: STRICT DECISION CRITERION NOT MET: the nodal MC (exact cKDTree, same sequential trimming rule as the protocol, N=50 new permutations) did NOT come within <1% of the real nodal retention (20 seeds) in any of the 8 g10b2 cells (error 4.3-5.1%) and in 5/8 g5b2 cells (error 1.4-2.6%; the other 3 met <1%: 0.04%, 0.25%, 0.67%). HOWEVER, an additional check (recomputing MC_nodal with the SAME 20 seeds as the nodal_real artifact) reproduced the declared value at 0.21% relative error -- ruling out a METHOD difference (exact cKDTree vs EDT) as the cause. The most likely cause of the remaining gap is SAMPLING NOISE: with sd~3.5% of retention across seeds and only 20-50 permutations, the estimated mean has a standard error of 0.5-0.8% PER SAMPLE, but the full distribution (individual values from 0.43 to 0.50 seen in the first seeds) is wide enough for two samples of 20-50 distinct seeds to disagree by 4-6% by chance. CONCLUSION (applying the pre-registered decision criterion literally): the granularity sentence CANNOT be stated as the measured cause of the original MC_blocos-vs-nodal_real gap (the <1% criterion was not met) -- it leaves the text for lack of support, BUT it is not replaced by a confirmed alternative cause; the additional finding (achado_adicional_sampling_variance) shows that the 4-6% gap may be entirely sampling noise from the few seeds (20) used for 'nodal real', which is a precision limitation of the nodal retention itself as cited in the text, not a physical property of the split.

nao_verificado.item: Q2 and Q4 (only Q1 and Q3 tested per cell, per city)
nao_verificado.motivo: checked in the summary of the nodal_real artifact BEFORE deciding the scope: Q1 and Q2 have IDENTICAL retencao_test.media (up to the 12th decimal place) in every cell/config, and Q3 and Q4 are also identical to each other -- but Q1/Q2 DIFFER from Q3/Q4 by ~0.3-1% (distinct geometries per pair). Running Q1 and Q3 covers the TWO distinct geometries of each city; Q2 and Q4 would exactly repeat Q1 and Q3.

achado_adicional_sampling_variance.descricao: sanity check outside the original scope of the decision criterion, done upon seeing that MC_nodal (exact cKDTree, seeds 1000-1049) and MC_blocos (continuous area) gave SIMILAR errors against nodal_real (20 seeds) at g10 (~4-5% both): the exact cKDTree method was recomputed using the SAME 20 seeds as the nodal_real artifact (42,1..19) for bauru Q1 g10b2 -- result: mean=0.46494, sd=0.03475, AGAINST the value declared in the nodal_real artifact (EDT) of 0.46591 (relative error 0.21%, within the tolerance <1e-3 already demonstrated at the gate of varredura_split_geometria.py). THIS RULES OUT a bug/discrepancy of METHOD between exact cKDTree and EDT. The cause of the MC_nodal(seeds 1000-1049) vs nodal_real(seeds 42,1-19) gap is SAMPLING NOISE: with sd~0.035 (bauru Q1 g10 test) and N=20 or N=50 permutations, the standard error of the mean is 0.78% (N=20) and 0.49% (N=50) RELATIVE TO EACH SAMPLE, but the DIFFERENCE between two independent samples has standard error ~2*sqrt(1/20+1/50)*sd = 0.93pp (~2% relative) -- still SMALLER than the 4-6% observed at g10, which suggests that the 20 seeds used in the nodal_real artifact (42,1,2,...,19) are NOT a large enough sample nor necessarily representative of the full distribution of retention per permutation (individual test retention values range from 0.427 to 0.498 in just the first 4 seeds tested) -- they are few and not clearly random (sequence 1..19, plus the production seed 42).
achado_adicional_sampling_variance.implicacao: the fixed decision criterion (MC_nodal <1% from nodal_real) was NOT designed to separate 'trimming rule' from 'sampling noise of few seeds' -- both would appear as a failure of the same criterion. Given that (a) the MC_nodal method uses the SAME sequential trimming rule as the protocol on real nodes and (b) matches the nodal_real artifact at 0.21% when it uses the SAME 20 seeds, the most parsimonious explanation for the failure of the criterion with N=50 NEW seeds is that N=20-50 permutations are TOO FEW to estimate the population mean retention to <1% (sd~3.5% of the mean, requiring N>~60 just for the standard error of ONE sample; to distinguish TWO samples at <1% with confidence, an even larger N would be needed -- outside the budget of this round). This does NOT confirm the granularity hypothesis (node-vs-block effect) nor refute it: it only shows that the test as defined cannot distinguish the two causes with the budgeted N. The granularity sentence therefore CANNOT be stated as a measured explanation (the strict criterion was not met), but there is also no POSITIVE evidence of granularity -- the remaining gap may be entirely sampling noise of the few seeds used in the 'real' nodal retention.
achado_adicional_sampling_variance.recomendacao: if the article needs a citable nodal retention number with <1% standard error, recalculate the 'real' nodal retention with N>=60 random seeds (not 20, not the sequence 1..19) before comparing with any MC; the current version of Tab. retention should report the nodal retention with its own CI (sd/sqrt(20)~0.8%), not as an exact point number.
